newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Maize Board details 96/97 export payments.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Maize Board details 96/97 export payments.

text.p: South Africa's state-run Maize Board said on Monday about 54 million rand remained in its export pools from last season and would be passed to deliverers as supplementary payments.
Preliminary figures show that sellers of white maize to the board's first pool would receive 27.00 rand a tonne, 30.00 rand a tonne for pool two and 53.00 rand for pool three.
On yellow maize deliverers would receive 24 rand a tonne for pool one, 38.00 rand for pool two and 50.00 rand for pool three.
Chairman Vic Mouton said that payments would be made around August 12 and that this would end the board's operational activities.

All South Africa's commodity control boards are required to wind down their activities following the passing of the Marketing of Agricultural Products Act last year. The Maize Board ceased all intervention in the country's maize market from the start of the season on May 1 this year.
